transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just have this constant restless feeling. It's like I'm wound too tight, and I just can't fully settle down. Even when I'm supposed to be calm—like sitting through a long planning meeting for work, or even when I'm trying to relax by painting or doing yoga—I just can't seem to shake it.
Have you had trouble sitting still like this since childhood?

Yes, I have. Um, I remember back in elementary school, my parents would get notes sent home pretty often. It was usually because I kept popping out of my seat during class. And I had a bad habit of talking over my classmates, or... rushing to blurt out an answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. So yeah, it's really been going on for a long time.
Did this restlessness start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Well, the restlessness itself has always been there, like I mentioned. But... it has been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. That's when some conflicts with my in-laws really started taking over more of our evenings. So the feeling didn't start then, but that situation definitely made it a lot harder to deal with.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things most days?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, the situation with my in-laws is frustrating, but I'm not really a worrier. I don't spend my days stressing over a bunch of different things. It's really just that physical restlessness I mentioned, rather than having a lot of anxious thoughts in my head.
Did your symptoms get better after the conflict with your in-laws ended?

Well, the conflict with my in-laws hasn't actually ended. It's still ongoing, so I can't really say if things would get better if it stopped. I'm still dealing with it, and the restlessness is still just as hard to manage.
Do you often have trouble focusing on tasks or following through on things you need to do?

No, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that. I mean... I'm a wholesale buyer, so following through on tasks and tracking orders is a big part of my day. I don't really find myself losing focus or leaving things half-done. It's really just that physical restlessness I was talking about, rather than an issue with getting my actual work finished.
Did your symptoms begin after the conflict with your in-laws started?

Yes, that's right. The restlessness has been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. That's right around the time the conflicts with my in-laws started taking over more of our evenings.
When the restlessness gets bad, do you also have episodes of sudden panic with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. My heart doesn't race or anything, and I don't get those feelings of panic. It's really just the physical need to keep moving, not a fearful or panicky feeling.
Do you get this restless, can’t-settle feeling in most areas of your life, or mainly when you’re dealing with the conflict with your in-laws?

It's really in most areas of my life, not just when I'm dealing with the in-laws. Um, at work, for instance, it's led to some corrected purchase orders, and my planning coordinator has had to start doing extra reviews of my stuff. And at home... well, it's made our regular family dinners a lot more tense, mostly because people feel like they're being talked over.
Before elementary school, do you remember having this same kind of restlessness or impulsive behavior?

Well, I definitely remember it being an issue in elementary school. I used to get notes sent home to my parents pretty regularly. It was mostly because I just couldn't stay in my chair—I kept popping up out of my seat during class. And I had a bad habit of talking over my classmates or blurting out answers before the teacher had even finished asking the question. So, yes, it's been around for a long time.
